analyst_view.overall: Early view: Leaders Almería won 1-0 at Girona through Miguel de la Fuente's eighth league goal and now face an Andorra side playing for the first time since the Tenerife match in which their goalkeeper Jesús Owono collided with Jesús de Miguel, who died the next day. Andorra asked for their game with Mallorca to be postponed because of the squad's emotional state; Owono faces a long ban (the disciplinary code allows four to 12 games, per one report), and the site also lists Lautaro De León and Efe Akman as suspended.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean a little lower: Almería's last three league games have been tight (1-0, 1-1, 2-2), and Andorra, without the suspended De León (three goals) and after a deeply difficult fortnight, may offer little going forward. A stand-in goalkeeper for the banned Owono is the main reason not to go lower still.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and I see no reason to move it. Almería should have the ball and most of the corners, while Andorra are likely to sit deeper than usual on the road; against the site's split those two effects broadly cancel out.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards, with Andorra expected to take 3.6 of them. I lean lower: after the events in Tenerife every Andorra challenge will be watched closely, and I expect a careful game from a squad one report described as deeply shaken. Almería, top of the table and at home, have little reason to make it physical.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. I lean lower: Almería's win at Girona came from just 12 shots per side, and their recent league games have been controlled rather than wide open. Andorra's attack is weakened by the bans to De León and Akman.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, a high figure for this division. I lean lower: Almería's recent games have been tight and Andorra are missing a regular scorer. If Andorra's replacement goalkeeper looks shaky Almería may test him often, which is the main risk to this lean.
